name: btor2
notes: Root of the hardware domain. BTOR2 bit-vector fragment, signed division family, and arrays (sort array, read, write, array ite, extensional eq/neq, constant-broadcast init, symbolic array inputs/states, nested arrays); no fairness/justice. Stimulus {"steps": [{"<node-id>": value, ...}, ...]}: one dict per frame for inputs, uninitialized states at frame 0, next-less states at any frame; missing entries are 0; an array node's value is an int (broadcast) or {"default": v, "set": {index: value}}. Observables {"bad": bool, "depth": int}: bad iff the property fires at some frame with every constraint holding up to it; depth = firing frame, else frames run. Era-6 revision 1 = the Era-5 btor2@3 text (lineage fable5-e870) re-cut and re-admitted; the trusted floor, graded stipulated, corroborated only by the domain anchors. Revision 2 ships the first certificate schema, `induction` (evidence/induction/check.py): a payload {"kind": "bit-invariant", "bits": [[state, bit, value], ...]} is discharged by three one-step SAT queries (init, consecution, safety), a payload {"kind": "k-induction", "k": K} by the base (BMC-unsat through K-1) and the step (one K+1-frame query from an arbitrary state); the judge is search-free, its budget a constant, and every failure path refuses the upgrade. The interpreter is byte-identical to revision 1 (conservativity: vectors and both bound pairs' corpora agree).
